title: Private Deploy Weekly: Surge Readout & Tuning Plan
summary: Week 6 pilot sync focused on last-week surge results, p95/p99 latency regression analysis after kernel upgrade, network egress shaping, and a concrete rollback + tuning plan. Agreed next steps: run a short canary with old kernel at peak window, update routing policy to prefer regional fallback, and Redwood to share a trimmed benchmark spreadsheet and SSO/KMS checklist.

transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-06-21 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen, Diego Alvarez, Priya Kumar (Redwood) — Evan Ross, Sofia Patel, Luca Romano, Janelle Wu (HelioMed)
Links referenced: https://redwood.ai/decks/pilot-ops (deck), https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/abcd (trimmed benchmarks)

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll run through the week six readout, quick status, then deep dive into the surge on tuesday and the kernel upgrade side effects. Diego and Priya are on for the technical bits, and then we will list out next steps.

[00:23] Evan Ross: thanks Maya, we expected the sprint to be smoother but the spike on tuesday was ... uh, not great. want to get to root cause and make sure the fallback doesn't add cost.

[00:40] Diego Alvarez: yeah hi all — quick context, we rolled kernel v1.5.0 Saturday at 02:00 UTC to improve continuous batching and some attention perf. baseline looked fine in small tests, but at production surge we saw p99 step up around the 95th percentile and some error retries.

[01:05] Sofia Patel: right, p95 went from ~120ms to 210ms and p99 from 480 to 900ms during the 30-minute spike. errors were mostly timeouts hitting our retry logic; we saw increased egress rates to region-b.

[01:32] Diego Alvarez: okay that's consistent with a few kernel optimizations that change the kernel's scheduling for KV cache reads — sometimes the new path introduces a stall under certain packet distributions. might be the attention kernel coupling with our batching pattern.

[01:58] Luca Romano: quick Q — are we sure it's the kernel and not the new routing policy you enabled? we did a couple of config tweaks last week to prefer regional burst pool.

[02:18] Diego Alvarez: good point, Luca. we instrumented both. stacktrace-level traces in the telemetry point to queue stalls inside the runtime on the GPUs, so primary suspect is kernel, but routing increased cross-region egress which amplified tail by hitting a slightly slower region. so both contributed.

[02:45] Priya Kumar: just to add — we correlate the traces with the routing logs; there were more cross-regional fallbacks during that 17:45-18:15 window which increased RTT slightly and increased token-level retries which then pushed the runtime into a different execution edge-case.

[03:12] Janelle Wu: from security side, we also noticed a higher number of KMS calls during retries; can that be contributing?

[03:25] Diego Alvarez: potentially yes, if retries re-request keys or re-init sessions the latency compounds. our recommendation is to keep a short-lived session cache and avoid per-request KMS fetches.

[03:42] Evan Ross: so immediate action is rollback kernel? or can we tune routing? what's lower risk?

[03:54] Maya Chen: we sketched two parallel tracks to reduce risk: 1) a quick canary rollback to kernel v1.4.8 for the peak window to confirm regression, 2) a routing policy adjustment to prefer local region primary with stricter circuit-breaker thresholds. both can be run in parallel, and Diego will provide the rollback playbook.

[04:20] Sofia Patel: timeline for the rollback? we need maintenance windows.

[04:30] Diego Alvarez: we can prepare the rollback playbook today, and we recommend running the canary during your next peak window Friday 18:00-19:00 UTC. it'll be a brief test — we'll only route 10% of traffic initially then expand.

[04:54] Luca Romano: sounds good. logging plan? i want to make sure we capture full traces for 10% and not sampling them out.

[05:05] Priya Kumar: we'll force 100% trace sampling for canary session ids and we will add additional event hooks for KV cache hit/miss metrics.

[05:22] Evan Ross: what about the egress shaping suggestion? earlier you mentioned QoS rules — can we rate limit to prevent spiky cross-region failover?

[05:35] Diego Alvarez: yes, egress shaping + adaptive backoff on the client side is recommended. on the platform we can apply token-bucket shaping at the edge and increase the grace threshold for circuit-breakers. but careful: overly aggressive shaping raises latency for real requests.

[05:58] Sofia Patel: is there a concise config diff we can review to understand the circuit-breaker thresholds?

[06:08] Maya Chen: yes Diego will share the config diff between your current profile and the suggested conservative profile. link will be in the trimmed spreadsheet.

[06:22] Diego Alvarez: i'll add the config diff and the kernel stack diff to the sheet. also i want to call out a small telemetry gap: some agent logs from your edge proxies were truncated during the surge so we don't have full QPS mapping for 17:50-18:05. Sofia if you can provide packet logs that will help.

[06:45] Sofia Patel: yep i can pull that and post it to the sheet, i'll include the pcap snippets.

[07:00] Janelle Wu: regarding KMS — are you using customer-managed keys or Redwood-managed? we did an initial KMS exchange last month but i want to verify cross-account CMK usage.

[07:12] Maya Chen: current pilot uses customer-managed KMS with a cross-account grant. we'll share the KMS checklist and Priya will coordinate the audit window.

[07:28] Evan Ross: curious on cost impact — did the fallback and retries materially increase billing? we had a spike in tokens and egress.

[07:40] Priya Kumar: preliminary numbers show a 12% increase in token compute during the 30-minute window, and egress storage transfers were up about 18% relative to baseline. Diego will post trimmed cost rows in the sheet so you can see per-token delta.

[07:58] Luca Romano: fine. can you remind us of the canary rollback steps? we want to ensure our runbooks cover host rotation etc.

[08:10] Diego Alvarez: high level: 1) create a canary pool with kernel v1.4.8, 2) deploy route rule to divert 10% traffic to canary pool, 3) enable 100% tracing for that pool, 4) monitor p95/p99 and error rates for 30 minutes, 5) if stable increase to 25% then 50% then fully. rollback steps reversed. we'll provide exact CLI commands and playbook.

[08:40] Evan Ross: are there known issues in v1.4.8 we should be aware of?

[08:48] Diego Alvarez: v1.4.8 lacks a couple of micro-optimizations for long-context attention that v1.5.0 introduced; in exchange it's more conservative on scheduling and has historically shown more stable tails under bursty traffic. it's a tradeoff of raw throughput vs tail predictability.

[09:10] Sofia Patel: ok that's acceptable for now. we prefer predictability.

[09:20] Maya Chen: we'll flag the recommended quantization and batching config as well — Luca, we noted your load pattern has a lot of short chats which benefit from smaller batch max and prefix cache tuning.

[09:36] Luca Romano: yes short chats, many sessions under 60 tokens. any batching suggestions?

[09:44] Diego Alvarez: bump concurrent request parallelism to lower latency and reduce the max batch size to avoid waiting. also enable prefix/KV caching aggressively for repeated user prompts — but careful with memory footprint.

[10:05] Janelle Wu: one more on security — when we run the canary, can audit logs be exported to our SIEM in realtime? we'll need that for compliance checks.

[10:16] Priya Kumar: yes we'll enable a real-time log-forwarding hook for the canary pool to your SIEM endpoint; we'll coordinate the webhook and ensure masking for PII.

[10:30] Evan Ross: great. let's talk about metrics we will watch during canary — what are the thresholds that will signal rollback?

[10:40] Diego Alvarez: primary triggers: p99 > 800ms sustained for >2 minutes, error rate >1.5% or increase in token retries >30% above baseline. secondary: spike in KMS latency >150ms per call. any trigger will auto-divert back to main pool and we'll escalate.

[11:05] Sofia Patel: sounds good. can Redwood push an automated alert to our ops channel?

[11:12] Maya Chen: yes we can configure alerting via webhook to your PagerDuty/Slack channel; we'll include runbook links in the alert payload.

[11:25] Luca Romano: after the canary and assuming rollback demonstrates stability, what's the remediation path? do we rework kernel or accept older kernel?

[11:36] Diego Alvarez: parallel path: while canary runs we will open an internal kernel investigation to isolate scheduling path, attempt a micro-patch to reduce the stall, and validate in a synthetic stress test. if we can patch within 2 weeks we plan to return to v1.5.x with fix; otherwise we'll keep v1.4.8 as stable until patch lands.

[12:00] Evan Ross: ok that timeline works. not ideal to run older kernel long-term but better than production instability.

[12:10] Priya Kumar: i'll also follow up with a telemetry map highlighting the missing logs and propose minimal agent changes to avoid truncation during surges.

[12:22] Maya Chen: excellent. quick check on documentation and artifacts — i'll email the trimmed benchmarks and the playbook links right after this call. Sofia, you will post the pcap and packet logs. Diego will post the config diff and the rollback steps. Janelle will confirm the KMS audit window.

[12:45] Evan Ross: any blockers on Redwood side?

[12:50] Diego Alvarez: only internal kernel issue tracking — we need to prioritize the micro-patch; i've kicked it off and will link the internal issue for transparency.

[12:58] Priya Kumar: i'll schedule the follow-up triage call for 2026-06-26 14:00 UTC and add agenda items for results from the canary.

[13:12] Maya Chen: great — recap of owners: Diego rolls the rollback playbook and config diffs, Maya shares spreadsheets and checklist, Luca and Sofia run canary and upload logs, Janelle confirms KMS constraints in writing.

[13:30] Evan Ross: thanks all. appreciate the quick turnaround.

[13:38] Maya Chen: thanks everyone — we'll follow up in email and see you next week.

[13:45] (meeting ended)

Notes on transcript quirks: some words auto-transcribed oddly — KV cache sometimes appears as 'K-V cash', kernel sometimes written 'kernal' in portions, and a few people's last names were mis-capitalized. This export retains the conversational style and occasional timestamps every few minutes for navigation.
